Coupled with a LiCoO2 cathode, the ASSLB delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 96.5% and an ultralong cycle life of 2000 cycles at room temperature, with a high output voltage of 3.84 V, outperforming state-of-the-art alloy-based counterparts. A practical all-solid-state pouch cell employing the LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode also delivers outstanding cycling stability. This work redefines alloy anode design principles through synergistic optimization of Li deposition potential and Li atomic diffusivity.

papers.title: From the Zoo to the BULLPEN: Sample-Efficient LLM Profiling via Multi-Channel Model Embeddings
papers.abstract: Choosing among the hundreds of thousands of available large language models (LLMs) requires a thorough understanding of each candidate model's properties. In practice, each property is measured by its own benchmark suite, so profiling a model on many properties means paying for many separate evaluations. To address this, model embeddings compress each model into a fixed-length vector from which many properties can be predicted. Existing methods, such as EmbedLLM, build these vectors from correctness patterns and question features, and often need large probe batteries to do so. However, many behaviors that are important when choosing a model, such as its verbosity, safety and style, show up more in how it answers than in whether it is correct. We introduce BULLPEN (Behavioral Understanding of Large Language models via Profile ENcodings), a framework that extends EmbedLLM in three ways. First, BULLPEN organizes the downstream tasks that prior work uses and adds 20 task benchmarks we built on behavior, style and provenance. Second, it is the first framework to read a model's own answer text jointly with its correctness and the question text. Third, it encodes models from a few hundred questions instead of the full 24,118-question pool. Across 260 open-weight models, our answer-text encoder scores 0.48 +/- 0.10 on the new tasks against 0.35 +/- 0.10 for the best prior encoder. Our encoders that read answer text keep at least 91% of their full-pool skill from only 400 questions (1.3% of the inference compute of the full question pool), while a correctness-only baseline keeps 83% with the same 400 questions. Because these embeddings need only model outputs, they support behavioral auditing and low-cost profiling, and could extend to API-only models. Code and data: https://github.com/wcquesera/bullpen

papers.title: From fleet trajectories to single-cell promises: hierarchically weighted conformal prediction for battery SOH monitoring
papers.abstract: Interval predictions from conformal prediction are usually read as "90% coverage", but on nested battery data that number promises the fleet average, not the individual cell. We measure the gap on 124 public LFP cells under a preregistered three-tier reporting protocol (fleet, batch, cell): pooled coverage looks healthy (0.875-0.906 across splits) while the worst cell is covered 0.1-2% of the time, with exact binomial tests against the nominal level. We then repair part of the gap with a hierarchically weighted conformal engine whose weights consume only side information frozen at prediction time - signature features, batch labels, cycle indices - and never touch residuals. The preregistered repair criterion passes: 10th-percentile cell coverage moves 0.750 to 0.830 (53% of the gap), the worst cell 0.642 to 0.694, with zero deferrals and a flat sensitivity spectrum. What the engine does not repair is localized rather than left open: under protocol drift the frozen weights harm monotonically on the SOH scale (the absolute scale is reported in full), a structural dead end we report instead of tuning away; and repair capacity is bounded by calibration-pool battery diversity, measured on both datasets. On a cross-chemistry external set the calibrated intervals collapse (0.286), while the within-domain skeleton replicates (pooled 0.933, worst cell 0.686). The deliverable is a reporting protocol - three tiers of promise anchored to measured regimes, worst-cell statistics, deferral share - that makes per-cell interval claims auditable before deployment.

papers.title: Kinetic Electrochemical Reactive-Transport Modeling of Calcium Leaching and Porosity Evolution in Multiphase Concrete
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Calcium leaching degrades concrete durability through progressive dissolution and decalcification of cement hydrate phases, yet it is commonly modelled by assuming local equilibrium between the pore solution and solid hydrates. While useful for estimating how much calcium is eventually depleted, such approaches do not fully resolve the kinetic coupling among hydrate dissolution, ionic transport within the bulk concrete and across the concrete-solution interface, and ultimately porosity evolution. Departing from local solid-liquid equilibrium, we couple dissolution-precipitation kinetics of calcium silicate hydrate, portlandite, ettringite, and monosulfate with multi-ionic diffusion and electrochemical migration in a unified concrete-solution domain, wherein interfacial ion concentrations emerge from flux continuity rather than prescribed fixed values. We reveal two coexisting Ca 2+ transport modes: (i) outward diffusion into the surrounding solution and (ii) accumulation at the active dissolution front, where Ca 2+ drives hydrate re-precipitation. The resulting near-surface porosity profile is non-monotonic, highest at the exposed surface due to dissolution, locally falling below the bulk value due to Ca 2+ -assisted re-precipitation, before recovering to a stable interior plateau. Lower w/c ratios reduce bulk porosity, whereas prolonged exposure extends the dissolution-dominated zone deeper into the concrete. Validated against long-term leaching profiles ( t = 3150 d; w/c = 0.30 and 0.55), the framework provides a mechanistic and experimentally grounded basis for predicting porosity evolution and strength degradation induced by calcium leaching in concrete.

papers.title: A novel method for mechanical battery abuse testing: Planetary mill calorimetric evaluation of all-solid-state battery materials and their safety
papers.abstract: This work presents a novel quantitative calorimeter-mill methodology for ASSB materials that quantitatively measures energy release by combining ball milling with calorimetry and pressure monitoring during extreme mechanical activation. The method accounts for the mechanical milling contribution using an operational reference. Applied to a shredded cathode consisting of delithiated state of charge 100% (SOC 100) Li x Ni 0.83 Mn z Co 0.17-z O 2 (x < 1, z < 0.17) (NMC), Al current collector, binder and conductive carbon together with systematically chosen amounts of Li 6 PS 5 Cl representing different catholyte compositions, the method quantifies composition-dependent energy release and gas evolution under extreme mechanical abuse. The method revealed that a shredded, delithiated NMC cathode showed substantial reactivity (2799 ± 159 J/g (NMC) ) with significant gas evolution, while Li 6 PS 5 Cl electrolyte addition enhanced the energy release and reduced the required mechanical activation and the gas generation. The calorimeter-mill approach provides a quantitative framework for establishing worst-case energy boundaries and enabling early-stage safety decisions in battery material development.

papers.title: FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction
papers.abstract: Battery degradation remains a central challenge in the development and broad application of sustainable energy technologies. Accurate degradation prediction is challenging, as battery aging emerges from complex and heterogeneous interactions among cycling behavior, operating conditions, and cell chemistry. Existing machine-learning approaches typically focus on deterministic end-of-life predictions or modeling degradation curves within fixed chemistry settings, leaving probabilistic state of health (SOH) trajectory modeling across heterogeneous chemistries underexplored. We introduce FlowBatt, a use-inspired conditional generative framework that adapts flow matching with a diffusion transformer (DiT) backbone to battery degradation trajectory modeling. FlowBatt models full SOH trajectories as probabilistic degradation processes conditioned on early-cycle capacity data. To strengthen this conditioning pathway, we use explainable AI analysis to diagnose and improve the encoder that maps early-cycle capacity matrices into conditioning vectors. We evaluate FlowBatt on five public benchmark settings spanning diverse chemistries and aging conditions, comparing it with supervised and diffusion-based trajectory models as well as established baselines for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction under shared data splits. FlowBatt achieves the best trajectory-wise SOH prediction performance on all five datasets, with errors below 2.5%, and delivers competitive RUL prediction performance. By generating multiple plausible trajectories, FlowBatt provides empirical prediction intervals for battery degradation modeling. These results indicate that flow-matching-based trajectory modeling is a promising framework for probabilistic battery health prediction.

papers.title: Ergotropy Activation and Coherence in Dissipatively Charged Quantum Batteries
papers.abstract: Quantum batteries can exploit quantum resources to enhance energy storage and work extraction, and recent experimental progress has brought their implementation closer to reality. In realistic settings, however, environmental dissipation is unavoidable, making dissipative charging a physically relevant operating regime. Here we investigate ergotropy in dissipatively charged quantum batteries, focusing on interaction-induced work extraction. For two coupled two-level systems (TLSs), we derive exact analytical expressions for the total, coherent, and incoherent ergotropy in both resonant and detuned configurations. We show that, in the resonant case, ergotropy is activated only above a critical coupling associated with an interaction-induced energy-level crossing, whereas detuning enables ergotropy already in the weak-coupling regime. Moreover, quantum coherence, although necessary for coherent work extraction, is not by itself sufficient to guarantee nonzero coherent ergotropy. In the strong-coupling regime, the resonant setup reaches the maximum ergotropy at a finite coupling strength, whereas the detuned setup approaches the same limit only asymptotically. Extending the analysis to a periodic XX spin chain of $N$ TLSs, we analytically derive the finite-temperature coupling threshold for ergotropy activation and show that it scales as $1/N$ in the large-$N$ limit. These results identify frequency detuning, interaction strength, and system size as key control parameters for ergotropy generation in open quantum batteries.

papers.title: Benchmarking Extended and Unscented Kalman Filters for Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Charge Estimation against a Physics-Based Virtual Cell: Effects of OCV Flatness, Initial Covariance and Temperature
papers.abstract: Kalman-filter state-of-charge (SoC) estimators are usually compared in simulations where the same equivalent circuit model (ECM) generates the data and runs inside the filter, and where errors are computed after the measurement update. Both practices flatter the estimators. This paper benchmarks Coulomb counting (CC), the extended Kalman filter (EKF) and the unscented Kalman filter (UKF) against a physics-based virtual cell: an experimentally parameterised Doyle–Fuller–Newman model of a 5 Ah LG M50 21700 cell with lumped thermal dynamics. A second-order RC ECM is identified from a simulated GITT/HPPC test (2.7 mV RMS fitting error) and then used, unchanged, by all estimators. The cell is driven by repeated UDDS and US06 cycles from 90 % to 10 % SoC at 10, 25 and 40 °C and in an aged state, with 10 mV voltage noise, 25 mA current noise and a 50 mA current offset. Errors are computed from the a priori estimate so that the initial error is always counted. With a correct initial SoC, both filters keep the RMSE between 0.39 % and 0.68 %, while CC drifts to 6.7 % over a 6.9 h UDDS test. A 300-run Monte Carlo study without SoC-limit effects shows that the two filters converge equally fast from under-estimated starts, but the EKF is markedly slower from over-estimated starts: with the recommended initial covariance its mean convergence time into a ±3 % band was 166 s (maximum 1110 s) against 1.2 s (maximum 2 s) for the UKF. All slow EKF runs started between 84 % and 93 % SoC, where the OCV slope of the cell falls to about 0.25 V per unit SoC; the EKF linearises at this flat point and applies too small a correction, whereas the UKF sigma points sample the steeper neighbouring regions. An initial covariance that is too small slows both filters by up to two orders of magnitude. At 10 °C, an ECM identified at 25 °C biases both filters by about −1 % to −2.5 %, which no filter tuning removes. The UKF costs about twice the computation of the EKF. The results show when the UKF is actually worth its cost and how the OCV shape of the specific cell should guide that choice.

papers.title: Covalent-Bond Engineering Stabilizes Layered Oxide Cathodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract Developing practicable layered oxide cathodes remains a critical challenge for sodium-ion batteries. Here, by systematically varying Cu contents to tune TM–O covalency in Nay[CuxFe3/9Mn(6/9–x)]O2, we show that an optimal degree of covalency simultaneously boosts energy density and structural resilience. The optimized Na7/9[Cu2/9Fe3/9Mn4/9]O2 delivers 131.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and retains 80% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. Mechanistically, the enhanced Cu–O covalency converts trivalent Cu from a conventional d8 to a heavily mixed d9L configuration, delocalizing holes across the extended TM–O network, enlarging polaron size, and “flattening the ripple” of local lattice distortions. Side-by-side comparison with an ionic Ni analogue confirms the suppressed cation migration and polarization. Crucially, the covalency-driven stabilization is not unbounded–excessive covalency rigidifies the lattice, defining a covalency threshold for optimal performance. These findings establish covalency modulation within a defined threshold as a predictive design principle for durable layered oxide cathodes.

papers.title: STEK: Structural-Terrain-Enhanced Koopman-Inspired Cross-Channel Regularization for Retrospective Battery Multi-Target Estimation
papers.abstract: Retrospective battery characterization across heterogeneous cells is challenging because cycling records vary substantially with chemistry, protocol, cell format, capacity, and operating conditions. An endpoint charge--discharge curve captures the local condition of an evaluated cycle, while a cell-level lifecycle terrain summarizes structural evolution across the archived trajectory. We propose STEK, a structural-terrain-enhanced framework for retrospective battery multi-target estimation. STEK combines a cell-level lifecycle (dQ/dV) terrain with an endpoint-derived structural proxy through quality-proxy-conditioned gating. Bounded FiLM and a validity-gated residual head refine the endpoint-curve representation while preserving a curve-based prediction pathway. Battery-type and optional material-text representations further condition an identity-centered low-rank linear map, providing a Koopman-inspired cross-channel consistency objective without modeling temporal dynamics or performing rollout. Under the fixed seven-output MIX-battery protocol, the full retrospective setting improves aggregate performance over endpoint-only learned baselines across multiple temporal backbones; this comparison reflects both the additional archived context and the modeling design. Under matched auxiliary inputs, STEK outperforms direct concatenation and quality-unaware FiLM, while descriptor-removal tests show graceful fallback to the endpoint pathway. Deterministic rules remain preferable for directly recoverable capacity summaries. The method targets retrospective archive harmonization rather than online estimation from cycle t alone.

papers.title: Higher-order topological quantum battery
papers.abstract: A quantum battery is a next-generation energy-storage device that exploits genuinely quantum properties such as superposition and coherence. We propose a second-order topological quantum battery coupled to a photonic crystal described by the breathing-Kagome model, where optical loss is present on all lattice sites while nonlinear gains are introduced selectively at the output sites. Under these realistic non-Hermitian conditions, the system exhibits a clear topological phase transition manifested in both the ergotropy and the charging power. Remarkably, perfect work extraction is realized in the topological phase, where the maximum value of the ergotropy is quantized and acts as a good topological-phase indicator. The triangular geometry coherently distributes energy into two quantum batteries, where mirror-symmetry-protected phase synchronization gives rise to collective energy storage.

papers.title: Physics-based modeling of cyclic and calendar aging of silicon-graphite composite anodes
papers.abstract: Higher energy density and longer lifetime are the requirements for next-generation lithium-ion batteries. A promising anode material is silicon, which offers high specific capacity, but its significant volume change during lithiation and delithiation enormously reduces battery lifetime. A physical understanding of the processes degrading the battery is key to mitigate this effect and advance in the field. We develop a physics-based model to describe degradation during battery cycling under various protocols and storage conditions (for C-rates ≤ 2 C, and temperatures T ≤ 35 °C), with varying check-up (CU) frequencies. The model can disentangle basic degradation mechanisms, such as the growth of the Solid-Electrolyte Interphase (SEI), from silicon mechanisms, such as particle cracking, SEI growth on cracks, and loss of active material (LAM). We investigate the impact of CUs on the observed storage degradation and the reason behind the increased degradation in batteries, including silicon in the anode. Additionally, we relate the observed degradation to operating conditions, enabling future optimization of battery use and design.

papers.title: Full-sunlight-driven photocatalytic recovery of critical metals from spent lithium-ion batteries via organic acid leaching
papers.abstract: The rapidly increasing deployment of secondary batteries has intensified pressures on resource security and waste management, exposing fundamental limitations of current battery recycling technologies that require intensive use of energy and chemicals. To enable sustainable battery waste management, systems must improve economic and environmental feasibility at the process level while retaining versatility toward diverse cathode chemistries. Here, we report a sunlight-driven photocatalytic leaching framework that enables robust recovery of critical metals from diverse commercial cathode materials. The process couples mild organic acids with a reusable photocatalyst to orchestrate a twofold leaching mechanism driven by sunlight, in which hydrogen peroxide is generated in situ across the solar spectrum and further activated by UV components to enhance metal extraction without external oxidizing agents. Importantly, the system maintains consistent performance over multiple operation cycles, supporting process robustness and scalability. Beyond its technical performance, techno-economic and life cycle analyses demonstrate clear advantages over conventional recycling methods, including lower energy inputs and reduced greenhouse gas emissions. This work establishes a versatile, profitable, and environmentally benign approach to battery recycling, offering a scalable pathway toward a sustainable circular economy. Researchers developed a light-driven method using organic acids to recover critical metals from used lithium-ion batteries, offering a more sustainable route for battery recycling powered by natural sunlight.

papers.title: Joint Electricity Price and Load Forecasting for Data Center Battery Dispatch Using Polynomial Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of large-scale data centers (DCs) is increasing electricity demand, market volatility, and operating costs. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) can mitigate these challenges by shifting electricity purchases from high-price to low-price periods. This paper proposes a real-time BESS dispatch framework using polynomial diffusion models (PDMs) to forecast both electricity prices and DC loads. Leveraging the closed-form conditional expectations of PDMs, the forecasts are integrated into a dynamic programming (DP) framework to minimize electricity procurement costs. Across the evaluated BESS configurations, the proposed approach achieves 2.63 times the cost savings of a rule-based (RB) strategy.

papers.title: Stay, Reposition, or Recharge: Battery-Aware Operation of Robotaxi Fleets
papers.abstract: Electric robotaxis are rapidly expanding from pilots to scaled commercial deployment; unlike traditional human-driven ride-hailing vehicles, they require centralized fleet control and careful management of vehicle state of charge (SoC). We study how a fleet manager should jointly make service, empty repositioning, idling, and charging decisions in such systems. We develop a continuous-time fluid model in which vehicles evolve across location-charge states, and identify two forms of charge-aware control that are absent from classic repositioning models: early return-to-depot (RTD) and charge-aware repositioning. In particular, the optimal solution admits simple threshold structures. Each location has a battery threshold such that vehicles should return to the depot to recharge when their SoC is below it and should not do so when their SoC is above it. Vehicles should not reposition below the same threshold either; above it, the choice of destination depends on whether a vehicle's SoC matches the destination's battery sensitivity, a notion we introduce in the paper. We then quantify the value of charge awareness by comparing fully charge-aware policies with charge-oblivious policies that ignore SoC in RTD and repositioning decisions. We show that the performance gap can be unbounded, driven by a dilemma between under-utilizing high-charge vehicles and over-sending low-charge vehicles to locations from which charging is costly. A numerical case study calibrated using 2025 NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission trip records illustrates these thresholds and shows that charge-aware control can generate substantial gains in a realistic urban network. Importantly, simple threshold-based heuristics recover most of the value of the fully charge-aware solution.

papers.title: Equivalent Circuit Model for Calculation of Ground Potential Rise in Wind Turbine Grounding Systems
papers.abstract: The ground potential rise caused by lightning is an important technical index for lightning protection design of wind turbines. A realistic approach is presented in this paper to calculate the ground potential rise in wind turbine grounding systems under lightning stroke. The electrical parameters of the grounding conductors are given by resistance, conductance, capacitance and inductance. The soil ionization due to dissipating lightning current can be taken into account by the effective radius estimated by the critical electric field intensity of soil ionization. According to the electrical parameters, the grounding conductors are replaced by π‐type circuit units and the circuit model is built for transient analysis of the single wind turbine grounding system and interconnecting configurations of multiple wind turbine grounding systems. The calculated results from the circuit model are compared with the measured ones to perform the model verification. Then, the circuit model is implemented into calculation of lightning transient responses in wind turbine grounding systems with attention to the ground potential rise. © 2026 Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan and Wiley Periodicals LLC.

papers.title: Coupling electrolyte mechanical reinforcement and interfacial stress relaxation for near-ambient sulfide all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
papers.abstract: All-solid-state lithium metal batteries offer the promise of higher energy density and improved safety compared with conventional lithium-ion batteries; however, their practical operation at room temperature and low stack pressures ( ~ 0.1 MPa) remains challenging due to lithium dendrite formation and stress-induced interfacial degradation. Herein, we demonstrate near-ambient operation ( ≤ 0.3 MPa, room temperature) of all-solid-state lithium metal batteries through a combined electrolyte–current collector design. A self-polymerizable thioctic acid-modified composite solid electrolyte suppresses internal lithium metal creep with high stress tolerance, while a porous carbon matrix current collector provides localized stress relaxation and accommodates lithium deposition within internal voids. As a result, stable long-term cycling is achieved under near-ambient conditions even at a high areal loading of 2.4 mAh cm−2 using a LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 positive electrode operated at 0.1 C. These findings highlight the importance of controlling lithium deformation and stress relaxation for the development of practical all-solid-state lithium metal batteries. All-solid-state lithium metal batteries can suffer from dendrite growth and interfacial stress at low pressures. Here, authors couple a self-polymerizable composite sulfide electrolyte with a porous carbon current collector, enabling stable near-ambient condition cycling at high areal loading.

papers.title: Degradation-Aware Participation of Battery Storage in Frequency Regulation Markets
papers.abstract: As data centers make the load on the power grid fluctuate faster, frequency regulation grows more valuable. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are well suited to provide frequency regulation, but providing this service speeds up aging, especially during operation at extreme state of charge (SoC). In the PJM interconnection, the grid operator supplies a regulation signal that a participating BESS is expected to follow, within a capacity that it must bid before the signal is known. Accordingly, we decompose the degradation-aware frequency regulation problem into a bidding layer and an operations layer. For bidding, we propose an adaptive strategy, assuming perfect tracking in which the bid depends on the SoC expected at the start of the bid period by means of choosing basepoints. For operation, the BESS further protects its battery by deliberately giving up a perfect performance score, to keep its SoC away from the extremes. On the PJM regulation signal and prices of 2023, adaptive bids lengthen the battery life by $31\%$ against bidding full capacity, for $2.2\%$ of the revenue. Giving up a perfect score in operation lengthens the battery life of constant bids by $10\%$ to $27\%$, at a change in revenue of at most $0.2\%$.

papers.title: Optimal performance of driven-dissipative many-body quantum batteries beyond complete nonreciprocity
papers.abstract: Proposals for nonreciprocal quantum batteries identify the point of complete nonreciprocity, where coherent and reservoir-mediated couplings balance, as the operating point for enhanced charging. We show that, for batteries built from interacting qubits, this point is, in general, suboptimal. The optimal design is set by a more intricate interplay between the coherent coupling and the local and collective dissipation rates, of which complete nonreciprocity is only a special case. We consider a many-body battery charged by a driven many-body charger, with each qubit coupled to a local bath and the complete setup immersed in a shared engineered reservoir. For a weakly driven two-qubit setup, we prove the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction to be the optimal coupling, and show that the battery capacity is maximized at a coupling strength fixed by the local and collective dissipation rates, which coincides with complete nonreciprocity only for a specific balance between them. The shared reservoir enhances the capacity for couplings weaker or stronger than both local dissipation rates, and can increase the extractable work even where it reduces the capacity. At strong drive, with the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction between the charger and the battery, the capacity is bounded by $1/2$. For qubits arranged in a star network with a single central battery qubit, these results remain qualitatively unchanged, while the maximum capacity of a battery charged by $N_A$ weakly driven charger qubits saturates with $N_A$ in the presence of the shared reservoir, approaching its limit as $N_A^{-1}$. In contrast, the maximum capacity of $N_B$ qubit batteries charged by a single-qubit charger decays as $N_B^{-2}$.

papers.title: Physics-Based Modeling and Validation of a Commercial Graphite-Lithium Manganese Iron Phosphate Cylindrical Cell Based on Teardown Derived Parameters
papers.abstract: Abstract Lithium manganese iron phosphate (LMFP) is an attractive cathode candidate for lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles, but physics-based simulations demand cell-specific parameter sets, which are still largely unavailable for commercial LMFP cells. In this study, we disassemble a commercial cylindrical graphite–LMFP cell and establish a self-consistent parameter set for Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) modeling. We determine cell geometry, composition, stoichiometry, and electrochemical properties using X-ray computed tomography, pseudo-open-circuit voltage measurements, the galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The resulting DFN model is assessed through OCV reconstruction, reference performance tests, GITT pulse–rest experiments, multi-rate CCCV charging protocols, and full-cell EIS. The calibrated model reconstructs the full-cell OCV with 3–5 mV RMSE, reproduces the complete continuous 1C pulse–rest discharge sequence with an RMSE of 41.60 mV, and captures CCCV charging from C/5 to 1.5C with overlap voltage RMSEs of 32.52–38.80 mV. It also recovers the low-frequency impedance response using a single, consistently constrained parameter set. This work delivers a reproducible parameterization methodology and a practical DFN reference model for graphite–LMFP cells.

papers.title: Nanostructure Engineering of Silicon-Based Anodes for High-Energy Lithium-Ion Batteries: Strategies, Performance, and Practical Challenges
papers.abstract: Because its theoretical capacity is significantly higher than that of traditional graphite, silicon is a desirable anode material for high-energy lithium-ion batteries. However, severe volume change, particle fracture, repeated disruption of the solid-electrolyte interphase, low electrical conductivity, and significant irreversible lithium loss limit its practical application. This paper investigates how nanostructure engineering and associated interface strategies address these coupled mechanical and electrochemical constraints. Stress accommodation, transport behavior, interfacial stability, and electrode packing are compared between low-dimensional silicon, porous and hollow particles, and core-shell or yolk-shell architectures. The complementary methods of surface coatings, artificial interphases, silicon/carbon composites, binder and electrolyte design, and prelithiation are then evaluated. Although areal loading, tap density, volumetric energy density, manufacturing yield, and compatibility with current electrode-processing techniques also affect practical performance, representative studies show that nanoscale control can significantly improve cycling stability, Coulombic efficiency, and rate capability. The analysis suggests that a multiscale design incorporating controlled internal void space, stable interfaces, conductive carbon networks, and manufacturable secondary particles is more promising than relying on a single nanostructure. First-cycle lithium loss, electrode swelling, process complexity, and scale-up are the remaining issues.

papers.title: Robust State-Parameter Estimation in Second-Order Thévenin Batteries
papers.abstract: We propose a scheme for estimating the full states and parameters of a second-order Thévenin battery model, using distinct features of the measured current. An identification step, run during suitable rest intervals, identifies the resistances and capacitances of the two RC branches from the voltage relaxation by linear least squares, without knowledge of the open-circuit voltage (OCV) map. An online estimator then runs continuously: the polarization voltages are estimated by open-loop observers; the series resistance is updated at current jumps using least squares; the state of charge (SOC) is propagated by Coulomb counting using the current capacity estimate, and both estimates are updated periodically by a sliding-window regression. We show that the identification is exact under a mild rank condition, that the series resistance is recovered at the first current jump, and that the online state and capacity estimates converge exponentially under verifiable excitation conditions. We also establish robustness of the online estimator under bounded process disturbances and measurement noise.

papers.title: How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
papers.abstract: Mixed-anion lithium oxychlorides exhibit high Li conductivity, but the relationship between oxygen content, structural framework, and Li-ion transport remains unclear. Here, crystal structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials are used to examine $\mathrm{Li}_yM\mathrm{O}_x\mathrm{Cl}_{6-2x}$ ($M$ = Nb and Ta [Group 5] and $M$ = Ti, Zr, and Hf [Group 4]). Increasing oxygen content changes isolated chloride-rich polyhedra into one-dimensional chains and subsequently more highly connected two- and three-dimensional frameworks. In the Group 5 series, fast Li diffusion occurs over $x \approx 0.67$--1.5, where the Li sites form a three-dimensional percolating network. Potential of mean force maps and nudged elastic band calculations reveal that fast Li-ion transport requires a low-dimensional framework supporting long-range migration through undercoordinated Li sites with low barriers, together with similar energies across Li sites. Finally, we perform fine-grid compositional search, which identifies $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{0.67}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.67}$, $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{0.75}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.5}$, $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$, and $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$ as stable candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities of up to $\sim 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{s}$. These findings establish how oxygen content controls framework and Li-ion transport, guiding the design of lithium oxyhalide electrolytes.
